If left_sum == right_sum, both pointers move inward; if left_sum < right_sum, left moves right and accumulates nums[left], incrementing operation count; otherwise right moves left. The greedy two-pointer strategy runs in O(n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.

Since all elements are positive integers, accumulating into the smaller sum is strictly necessary to equalize left and right outer sums. Absorbing adjacent elements corresponds directly to 1 merge operation per step until pointers meet.
Both pointers move inward until left >= right, taking at most n steps in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
